blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how businesses measure their financial health? Accounting ratios can tell a story about a company's profitability, liquidity, and efficiency.

blocks.markdown: Accounting ratios are essential tools used to evaluate the financial performance of a business. They help stakeholders understand how well a company is doing in terms of profitability, liquidity, and efficiency.

blocks.title: Definition of Accounting Ratios
blocks.text: Accounting ratios are quantitative measures derived from financial statements to assess various aspects of a company's performance.

blocks.markdown:
### Profitability Ratios
Profitability ratios measure a company's ability to generate profit relative to its revenue, assets, or equity. Key ratios include:
- **Gross Profit Margin**: Indicates the percentage of revenue that exceeds the cost of goods sold.
- **Net Profit Margin**: Shows the percentage of revenue remaining after all expenses.
- **Return on Capital Employed (ROCE)**: Measures the efficiency and profitability of a company's capital investments.

blocks.title: Calculating Gross Profit Margin
blocks.prompt: A company has a revenue of ₦500,000 and a cost of goods sold of ₦300,000. Calculate the gross profit margin.

steps.text: Calculate the gross profit: Revenue - Cost of Goods Sold = ₦500,000 - ₦300,000 = ₦200,000.
Calculate the gross profit margin: (Gross Profit / Revenue) × 100 = (₦200,000 / ₦500,000) × 100 = 40%.

blocks.markdown:
### Liquidity Ratios
Liquidity ratios assess a company's ability to meet its short-term obligations. Important ratios include:
- **Current Ratio**: Compares current assets to current liabilities.
- **Acid-Test Ratio**: Similar to the current ratio but excludes inventory from current assets.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When calculating ratios, ensure all figures are from the same financial period to maintain accuracy.

points: Profitability ratios help assess how well a company generates profit.
Liquidity ratios evaluate a company's ability to pay off short-term debts.
Understanding these ratios can provide insights into a company's financial health.
